subject: CAPEX vs OPEX thresholds for LLM usage and procurement path
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: CAPEX vs OPEX thresholds for LLM usage and procurement path

Ian / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Short recap and next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what you shared
- Expected pilot: ~3M to 8M tokens/month (text gen + embeddings) initially, with potential scale to ~30M+/month in 12 months if latency and cost profile hold.
- Procurement constraints: finance distinguishes capital (one-time install/ HW) vs operational spend (monthly SaaS). Current bar for raising a PO is ~$50k / month (net), above that requires procurement lead time and an internal approver.

Primary asks from your side
1) Can we provide a clear $/1M token target for the pilot (best-effort range depending on model/quantization)?
2) Recommended procurement trigger: what monthlyBand should you plan for to safely move to a PO vs shorter credit agreement?
3) Any SOW/PO templates and high-level timelines we should feed to procurement.

What we will deliver by EOD Mon (Sep 27)
- A short table with model + quantization scenarios and an estimated $ / 1M tokens (pilot and scaled bands).
- Suggested procurement thresholds (recommended PO cadence vs monthly billing, and lead times).
- Pricing sheet (attached) and a starter SOW template for procurement to review.

Attachment note: the pricing sheet I referenced is attached as "redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.pdf" (line items + optional reserved capacity corridors). SOW template is attached as well.

Proposed next steps
- Naomi to send the price/threshold table (Mon).
- Ian to confirm whether procurement prefers a single annual PO or monthly charge with a rolling commitment.
- If PO required, we can engage our Partnerships/legal team to pre-fill SOW and speed approvals.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
https://redwood.com
From: Ian Carter <ian@dataworks.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAPEX vs OPEX thresholds for LLM usage and procurement path

Naomi — thanks for the recap. Couple clarifications from procurement/finance: 
- The $50k/month PO threshold is a hard trigger for our AP team: above that they require a signed PO and at least two weeks of lead time.
- Our finance team treats cloud/hosted platform fees as OPEX, but if there is any hardware charge or large one-time integration fee they will push it into CAPEX and route through a different approval chain (longer).

On the $/1M tokens: what matters for our budget is the blended effective rate across the workload (most tokens will be short chat turns, but about 20% will be long generations ~1k tokens). We need a pilot target that is defensible to our CFO — ideally a conservative upper bound we can quote.

We can confirm procurement preference after you send your suggested bands. For now, treat us as: 
- Pilot band: commit to monthly billing until we validate latency and quality (~3–8M tokens).
- If monthly spends trend above $50k consistently over two months, we will move to a PO.

I will loop in procurement if you send a sample SOW/PO language.

Thanks,
Ian
DataWorks — Head of Platform
ian@dataworks.io
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ian Carter <ian@dataworks.io>, Priya Rao <priya@dataworks.io>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAPEX vs OPEX thresholds for LLM usage and procurement path

Ian / Priya — attaching the short pricing table and an explanation of the assumptions (see attachments). High level notes below: 

Assumptions that drive $ / 1M tokens
- Model mix (pilot): 70% small chat model (approx 60B quantized), 30% occasional long-gen on a larger model.
- Quantization: 8-bit int where possible, yield ~1.8x token cost savings vs fp16 on our serving runtime.
- Caching/prefix reuse: expected to reduce billable tokens for prompts by ~12% for chat flows.

Estimated effective pricing (conservative) — pilot band (3–8M tokens/mo):
- Conservative blended: $430 / 1M tokens
- Aggressive (optimistic optimizations + reserved capacity): $280 / 1M tokens

Scaled band guidance (20–40M tokens/mo):
- Suggest procurement plan: once expected spend > $50k/month for two consecutive months -> convert to a PO and consider a reserved capacity discount (we can propose 10–20% off list depending on committed slab).

Procurement/PO path suggestion
- Up to $50k/month: recommend monthly billing (SaaS OPEX) with 30-day payment terms (fastest path).
- $50k–$150k/month: suggest a 6–12 month reserved capacity commitment with a PO; this shortens lead times and ensures consistent latency.
- >$150k/month: enterprise contracting, multi-region redundancy, and SLA addendum (longer legal cycles).

Attachments included: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.pdf (line-item calc), redwood-sow-template.docx (starter SOW), and a short Drive playbook URL with example clause language.

Example math (conservative): 5M tokens/mo x $430/1M = $2,150/mo (pilot) — note this is net of token reductions from caching for chat. If usage grows to 40M tokens/mo we would recommend a reserved commit with a quoted unit price nearer $260/1M and a monthly effective spend ~ $10,400/mo (after discount).

If this looks good we'll generate a one-page procurement summary you can hand to finance (SOW + example PO language).

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachments:
- redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.pdf (pricing table, per-model assumptions)
- redwood-sow-template.docx (starter SOW)
